newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Structural reform needed for Europe employment - G10.
newsitem.headline: Structural reform needed for Europe employment - G10.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer told reporters after a meeting of G10 central bankers that long-term structural reform was needed to address high unemployment in Europe.
Tietmeyer said Europe especially had problems in the area of employment. He noted unemployment differed from country to country "but in most countries it is relatively high".
The G10 discussed structural reforms "because there is a clear understanding most unemployment is of structural nature", he said.
Tietmeyer said he hoped economic growth would help solve some of the unemployment problem but at the same time structural issues had to be addressed in a convincing way that had a lasting impact.

G10 governors also discussed the impact of current budget consolidation in Europe, he said. "I think it is necessary to continue consolidation of budgets. It is important there are substantial and lasting improvements," Tietmeyer said.
He said the lasting budget consolidation efforts were necessary to create confidence for private investors to invest in European countries and thus create new jobs and employment.
He also noted that labour market reform was needed.

G10 central bankers also discussed Europe's preparations for economic and monetary union and were briefed by Alexander Lamfalussy, president of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner to the future European central bank.

"There is a clear convergence as far as inflation and long-term rates (are concerned), but the problem is still in the budget field," he said, adding a lot of effort was necessary to create a lasting and sustainable situation as far as budgetary and debt situations are concerned.
He noted the decision on which countries would qualify for EMU would be made next year along the lines of the Maastricht Treaty criteria.
The G10 did not discuss in detail where countries stood as regards meeting the criteria, he added.
